title: Rust compress writes out buffer before failing: error returns leave partial bytes (decompress is atomic)
description: Confirmed empirically (discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-xuc8, robustness pass). compress_mqtt_sn (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:1014-1047) sets out[0]=RULE_MQTT_SN (:1017), zero-fills out[1..] via BitWriter (:143), writes residue and copies tail BEFORE the needed>out.len() check (:1044); enforce_encoded_profile_limit (:2161) fires only after full encoding written. Probe: input needing 121 bytes with 25-byte out -> Err(BufferTooSmall) with all 25 bytes modified, out[0]=0x07; over-profile input with 40000-byte out -> Err(profile limit) with all 40000 bytes written. decompress side is fully atomic on error (0 bytes modified) and Python is atomic by construction. No current in-repo caller reads out after Err (checked link.rs:263, decompress_authenticated_frame_tracked) so impact is latent, but the compress/decompress asymmetry is undocumented and any caller assuming error implies untouched buffer gets stale/garbage bytes. Fix: size-check before first write in compress_mqtt_sn (and audit other per-rule compress fns for the same pattern), or document the contract explicitly plus a regression test asserting buffer-untouched-on-error.
